_comment: Skip-list for `zig build wasi-testsuite`. After PR #661 made `wamr run` AOT-only (#644), every C and Rust wasm32-wasip1 fixture and ~half of the AssemblyScript fixtures failed because the AOT pipeline did not yet handle production wasm binaries (out-of-bounds memory access early in `_start`, AS runtime asserting at startup). Tracked in #662, which landed the AOT fixes; re-audited 2026-07-10 and all but one C fixture, all Rust fixtures, and 2 of 3 AssemblyScript fixtures now pass — see `tests/wasi-conformance-audit.md`. Suite keys match the `name` field in each `tests/wasi-testsuite/tests/<lang>/testsuite/wasm32-wasip1/manifest.json` (note the double space in the AssemblyScript suite name — that's upstream). P3 has its own gate at `tests/wasi-p3-testsuite-skip.json` (still broken — unrelated cross-instance async-builtin gap, see #881). See `tests/wasi-conformance-audit.md` for the audit log.

WASI C tests [wasm32-wasip1].clock_gettime-monotonic: Flaky upstream fixture, unrelated to AOT/JIT: `clock_gettime-monotonic.c` compares two `clock_gettime` reads' `tv_nsec` fields directly (`ts1.tv_nsec < ts2.tv_nsec`) without accounting for `tv_sec` rollover, so it intermittently fails whenever the two reads straddle a second boundary. Reproduces under both the two-step AOT path and the in-process JIT path at similar rates — confirmed not a wamr regression.

WASI Assemblyscript tests [wasm32-wasip.environ_sizes_get-no-variables: wamr CLI inherits host environment when no `--env` flags are passed; the wasi-testsuite harness expects an empty environ for this case. Tracked separately from #662 Phase B — Phase B fixed the AOT startup abort that previously masked this.
